title: Outbox pattern
description: Learn the outbox pattern for reliable event publishing. Understand how to guarantee that database updates and message publishing happen atomically.

data.text: The outbox pattern solves the problem of reliably publishing events when database updates occur. It ensures that a message is published for every database transaction, preventing lost events.
The Problem: Dual Write
Updating a database and publishing a message are two separate operations. Without coordination, failures can cause inconsistency.

items: Update succeeds, publish fails—event lost
Publish succeeds, update fails—invalid event
Both succeed—correct state
Network failures cause either scenario
Distributed transactions are expensive

data.title: No Atomic Operations
data.text: You can't atomically update a database and publish to a message queue. They're separate systems with separate transactions.
The Outbox Pattern
The outbox pattern stores events in an outbox table within the same database transaction as the business data.

items: Write business data and outbox entry in same transaction
Both succeed or both fail—atomic within the database
Separate process reads outbox and publishes to message queue
Delete outbox entry after successful publish
Guarantees event delivery if the database update succeeds

data.title: Key Benefit
data.text: The outbox pattern converts a distributed transaction problem into a local transaction problem, which databases handle reliably.
How It Works
Step 1: Write to Outbox
In the same transaction as your business logic, insert an event into the outbox table.
Step 2: Poll Outbox
A background process polls the outbox table for unpublished events.
Step 3: Publish Message
Publish the event to the message queue, then mark it as published in the outbox.
Implementation Considerations

items: Use idempotent message publishing to handle duplicates
Implement transactional outbox reader for cleaner implementation
Consider CDC (Change Data Capture) as an alternative
Clean up processed outbox entries to prevent table bloat
Monitor outbox size and processing lag

data.text: Transactional Outbox
Some databases support transactional outbox patterns natively or through extensions.

items: PostgreSQL: LISTEN/NOTIFY for real-time notification
SQL Server: Service Broker integration
Debezium: CDC-based outbox pattern
Oracle: Advanced Queuing
Extension libraries for transactional messaging

data.title: CDC Alternative
data.text: Change Data Capture can read the transaction log and publish events automatically. This eliminates the need for an explicit outbox table.
Trade-offs

items: Pros: Reliable event delivery, no distributed transactions, simple to understand
Cons: Additional database table, background process needed, eventual consistency
Database load: Outbox table adds read/write load
Complexity: Requires careful implementation of the polling process

data.text: When to Use
Use the outbox pattern when event delivery is critical and you can't tolerate lost events.

items: Critical business events that must be published
Systems with strong consistency requirements
When you need to guarantee event ordering
When message delivery failures are unacceptable
As an alternative to distributed transactions
